_about: Hand-drawn lake polygons ABSENT from the FWA waterbody layer, ingested as real lake nodes. See pipeline/hack/added_lakes/README.md for the wbk minting scheme and the one thing that makes a lake a lake: the fids inside the polygon are re-stamped with its wbk, which is what breaks the stream run and mints the lake:{wbk} boundary.

properties.name: Redsand Lake
properties.note: DFO Region 6 scope B(ii) regulates 'Redsand Lake' including tributaries (coho 4/day only 1 over 50 cm Sep 1-Oct 31; no fishing for chinook all year). FWA has no polygon for it, so no water of that name exists at all — an exact lookup for 'Redsand Lake' returns nothing. Treston Lake, 441 m south, carries the name variant 'TRESTON LAKE  REDSAND LAKE' from a BATHYMETRY map label (source: bathymetry in name_variants.json) — a sheet covering both lakes, which is itself evidence they are two waters. It indexes only under its own full string, so Treston never answered to 'Redsand Lake'; a substring search suggests otherwise and is not how the matcher works. Sits on the Kitsumkalum River (blk 360883243, wsc 400-195432) in the section 'between Treston Lake and Kitsumkalum Lake' — the same river Treston sits on, 441 m north of it. Hand-drawn, supplied by the curator 2026-09-01, EPSG:3857 -> 4326. 40.49 ha, 25 vertices, centre 54.70592/-128.77963, MU 6-15. Synthetic ids: wbk -1, gnis -9000001 — both NEGATIVE, and the gnis is beyond the real range in magnitude (real gnis run 1,642..8,000,027) so it cannot be confused with a real id even if a sign is lost.

claims.note: unnamed tributary, ~228 m inside — the lake swallows its mouth
